question: Should Gateway browser-origin authorization support scheme-wide entries such as `chrome-extension://*`, and if so what constrained grammar and security review should define that contract?
rationale: The requested behavior broadens an origin authorization boundary beyond exact matches and the existing global wildcard, so automation should not choose the permanent security grammar.

options.title: Approve constrained scheme patterns
options.body: Define a narrow grammar for specific schemes, update `checkBrowserOrigin`, docs, config help, and security tests around that contract.

options.title: Prefer exact custom-scheme origins only
options.body: Keep scheme-wide wildcards rejected and steer fixes toward exact non-standard origin matching such as the linked custom-scheme PRs.

options.title: Reject core support
options.body: Keep the current exact/global-only contract and require extension relay operators to manage exact origins or use a plugin-owned gateway surface.

recommendation.title: Approve constrained scheme patterns
recommendation.body: Define a narrow grammar for specific schemes, update `checkBrowserOrigin`, docs, config help, and security tests around that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history signal for the Gateway origin security boundary and prior non-loopback origin policy changes.
